record.paper_title: Problems in Data Structures and Algorithms
record.original_question: Given two binary search trees with the same n ordered keys, determine the minimum number of rotations needed to transform one tree into the other. In particular, is there an efficient algorithm for computing this rotation distance exactly, or is the problem computationally intractable?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1 Given two n-node trees, how many rotations does it take to convert one tree into the other?
This question seems to be NP- hard.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A rotation in a binary search tree is the standard local restructuring operation that, given an internal edge between a node and one of its children, exchanges their parent-child relationship while preserving the in-order sequence of keys. Two binary search trees on the same n ordered keys can always be transformed into each other by a finite sequence of rotations; the rotation distance d(T, T') between two such trees is the minimum number of rotations needed to transform T into T'.

Determine the computational complexity of computing the rotation distance: given two binary search trees T and T' on the same n ordered keys (equivalently, two rooted binary trees with n internal nodes and a fixed in-order labeling), is there a polynomial-time algorithm that computes d(T, T') exactly, or is this decision/optimization problem NP-hard?
artifact.status_search_result: The exact computational complexity of computing rotation distance between two binary trees remains open. The problem is known to be in NP, fixed-parameter tractable in the distance k, and has constant-factor approximation algorithms, but no polynomial-time exact algorithm or NP-hardness proof is known. Closely related problems such as flip distance between triangulations of a simple polygon and shortest paths on graph associahedra have been shown NP-hard, but these results do not settle the rotation distance question for general binary trees.

status_evidence.title: Rotation distance - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The computational complexity of computing the rotation distance is unknown... it is not known to be NP-complete, nor is it known to be solvable in polynomial time.
status_evidence.claim: The exact complexity of rotation distance between binary trees is open.

status_evidence.title: Hardness of Finding Combinatorial Shortest Paths on Graph Associahedra
status_evidence.snippet: Computing a combinatorial shortest path between two vertices of a graph associahedron is NP-hard.
status_evidence.claim: Related associahedron shortest-path problems are NP-hard, but this does not resolve the rotation distance question.

status_evidence.title: Rotation Distance is Fixed-Parameter Tractable
status_evidence.snippet: Rotation distance is fixed-parameter tractable in the distance parameter k.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive results (FPT, approximation) exist but exact complexity remains open.
